name: COMOROS
lead: Comoros is a small group of islands in the Indian Ocean, between Madagascar and Africa. Its name means "Islands of the Moon" in Arabic. Each of its three main islands has a volcano.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Built at foot of an active volcano

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Comoros was born of fire. Grande Comore has Mount Karthala, an active volcano. Its crater is over 3 km wide. A small town could fit inside.
Coral reefs ring the islands. On Mohéli, the smallest island, forest grows down to the beach, where sea turtles nest.
animals: The coelacanth is a fish that hides in deep caves off Grande Comore. It grows up to 2 metres long.
Livingstone's fruit bat has wings 1.4 metres wide. Each island also has its own tiny scops owl, found nowhere else on Earth.
culture: The Grand Mariage (Big Wedding) is the biggest event in a Comorian life. This wedding party lasts two weeks, with feasts, dances and sultan-style costumes. Families save for years.
Music called twarab mixes the Arabic lute (a string instrument), the violin and Swahili poetry. For celebrations, women paint their faces with golden sandalwood paste called msindzano.
history: Arab traders brought Islam around the 10th century. They named the islands Juzur al-Qamar. Rival sultans (Muslim kings) ruled each island and traded spices across the sea.
France took control in the 1800s. Independence came in 1975. Then came more than 20 coups (attempts to seize power) in 50 years. People called them 'the coup-coup islands'.
wows: Comoros supplies about 80% of the world's ylang-ylang oil, used in perfume.
Mount Karthala, one of Earth's most active volcanoes, erupts about every 11 years, last in 2007.
Comoros has had over 20 coups (power grabs) since 1975, more per person than almost any country.
A live coelacanth, a fish thought gone for 65 million years, was caught here in 1938.
Moroni, the capital, is one of very few capitals built on an active volcano's lava field.
Livingstone's fruit bat lives nowhere else on Earth, and fewer than 1,500 survive.
In 2001, Mohéli island opened Africa's first community-run sea park south of the Sahara.

myths.fact: No. They are two countries about 300 km apart, each with its own president.
Vanilla is a climbing orchid. Farmers pollinate each flower by hand. Comoros grows it.
